blocks.text: Cloverdale Farms: what the ground is and what governs it

items.t: Live-page editorial scope (site copy, not adopted as fact): the page describes Cloverdale's agricultural belt as spanning the Serpentine and Nicomekl lowlands west of 176 Street and south of Highway 10, with hobby farms near 168 Street / 40 Avenue and larger berry, nursery, forage and vegetable operations.

blocks.text: Local rules that affect acreage buyers

items.t: Suites / coach houses: Surrey's urban rule is one secondary suite per single-family, semi-detached or duplex dwelling unit, at most 40% of the principal unit's habitable floor area, never inside a coach house or garden suite and not a separate strata lot; coach houses / garden suites run 35–75 m² (up to 120 m² on RA, R2, R2-O and R3 lots below maximum FAR) with one extra parking space. On ALR land the ALC rule above is the stricter frame (suite inside the principal residence only). Whether a Surrey coach house can serve as the ALR "additional residence" on a given parcel is a parcel-level ALC + City check: Not verified as a general rule. Surrey SSMUH (3 / 4 / up to 6 units by lot band, Jul 8, 2024) is an urban-lot framework — it is not a route to extra dwellings on ALR farm parcels.

The page's farm-class summary understates the rule it summarizes: "$2,500 to $10,000+" flattens a three-tier test whose middle tier is a formula ($2,500 plus 5% of value over 4 ha) — a mid-size operation priced on the flat summary will misstate its qualification income.
On Serpentine lowland ground those are per-parcel City and title checks, not page facts — budget the diligence, not the copy.

Cloverdale's farm land is the lowland east and south of the town centre, in the City of Surrey, around 176 Street (Highway 15) and Colebrook Road.
The Serpentine River lowland is the named farm landscape here: Surrey's 72 Avenue project crosses the Serpentine River and Bear Creek to reach agricultural land in this belt.
Cloverdale began at Five Corners, the historic intersection of 60 Avenue and Old McLellan Road, established in 1879 in the Clover Valley agricultural area.

blocks.text: Cloverdale Farms: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Sensitive-ecosystem review can apply on a farm lot: the 3073 – 184 Street proposal paired its setback variance with a Development Permit for Sensitive Ecosystems.

blocks.text: Cloverdale Farms: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: Farm ditches are part of the road design here: Surrey's 72 Avenue extension promises improved agricultural ditches and full-movement farm access, not just lanes.

Barn Owl habitat is a named constraint east of the Serpentine River: Surrey's environmental assessment for 72 Avenue identifies Barn Owl, a species at risk, with critical habitat near the corridor where barns provide suitable habitat.
Salmon-bearing water runs through the farm belt: Bear Creek, Fleetwood Creek and the Serpentine River are all identified as salmon-bearing in the same City assessment.
Normal farm practice protection applies to the working farms around the town centre, through the BC Farm Industry Review Board (BCFIRB) complaint process.

blocks.text: Cloverdale Farms: development and new projects

items.t: 72 Avenue Improvements & Extensions, Fraser Highway to 184 Street, City of Surrey: four-lane extension with agricultural ditch improvements and a Serpentine River bridge. Status: preloading from 152 Street to 156 Street began summer 2025; road anticipated complete in 2031; the 188 Street to 196 Street widening is anticipated complete in fall 2026 (as of November 3, 2026).

Cloverdale Town Centre Plan Update, City of Surrey: plan update to support the new hospital and BC Cancer Centre near the town centre. Status: Council authorized staff to initiate the update on October 30, 2023 (check current) (as of November 3, 2026).
Surrey's 2026 Municipal Total tax rate is 1.84251 per $1,000 for Class 1 Residential and 4.48750 per $1,000 for Class 9 Farm, per the City's 2026 property tax rate schedule.
Surrey also charges a Capital Parcel Tax of $300.00 for Class 1, 8 and 9 properties, collected with property taxes, per the 2026 schedule.
The 72 Avenue extension is designed as a continuous east–west route from 120 Street to 196 Street, with full-movement intersections at 152 Street, 168 Street and Highway 15.

blocks.text: Cloverdale Farms: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the ditch and creek lines on the lot: the City's own assessment names the Serpentine River, Bear Creek and Fleetwood Creek as salmon-bearing, with bridges and large culverts planned where 72 Avenue crosses them.
The ALR check does not settle tax class: BC Assessment classifies on production for sale, not on ALR status alone.

faq.a: No — under the ALC housing rules a secondary suite is permitted only inside the principal residence; a detached second dwelling is the "additional residence," which is size-capped under the 90 m² / 186 m² limits.
faq.q: Can a suite go in a barn or a detached building on a Cloverdale farm?

faq.a: Bed-and-breakfast use inside a lived-in principal residence is permitted within the ALC's four-bedroom / 30-day limits.
faq.q: Can I Airbnb the farm house?

faq.a: One principal residence per parcel is permitted without an ALC application at a maximum total floor area of 500 m², with no more than 1,000 m² of fill placed for its construction; anything larger requires ALC approval, and the City may regulate further.
faq.q: How big can a house be on ALR farmland in Cloverdale?

faq.a: One additional detached residence may be permitted without an ALC application where the conditions are met — maximum 90 m² on parcels of 40 ha or less, or 186 m² on parcels over 40 ha — and City of Surrey bylaws must also permit it.
